absent: Numeric values of user and kernel selectors, EFLAGS bits, MSR numbers, CET enable bits, RPL masks, syscall numbers, and personality and address-space flag bits.
Initial shadow-stack enable path, contents of thread shadow-stack state, and behavior of feature query and set helpers and shadow-stack free.
Contracts of floating-point, TLS, paravirtual, cache-allocation, stack-update, sysenter-refresh, FSGS and current-task helpers including sleeping and ordering rules.
Meanings of thread-flag work masks, conditional STIBP branch state, and work performed by the extra-switch worker.
Virtual-8086 IRQ range bounds, table element layout, lock initialization, and interrupt allocation and free contracts.
Trap-frame and user register structure layouts, segment base handling under FSGSBASE, PKRU register semantics, and CR3 LAM mask and untag-mask construction.
FRED saved-state layout, debug-entry hard-interrupt stack tracking, AMD workload and null-segment errata details, and compat versus x32 ABI selection beyond the fragments.

findings.text: The kernel exposes a thread teardown hook for a terminating task in both 32-bit and 64-bit builds. The 32-bit variant requires that no address space remains and then releases virtual-8086 interrupt associations owned by the task. The 64-bit variant only checks for a lingering address space with a warning.

User thread entry setup is exposed through 32-bit, 64-bit and compatibility entry points sharing a common 64-bit helper. They program user code, data and stack selectors together with instruction pointer, stack pointer and interrupt-related flags so that the next return enters user mode at the requested address.

Task context switching is exposed per architecture. Each variant preserves outgoing floating-point and segment state, installs incoming TLS, segments, protection-key and mitigation state, refreshes kernel stack and current-task records, and returns the outgoing task.

Execution personality control and CET thread-state reset are exposed. One entry establishes 64-bit mode, another selects 32-bit compatibility or x32 mode, and a reset helper clears shadow-stack bookkeeping and feature control fields in the current thread.
Tracing helpers translate between trap-frame register names and byte offsets in both directions, and a virtual-8086 helper releases every interrupt binding owned by a supplied task.
An unimplemented system call entry is provided that unconditionally reports the not-implemented error to the caller.

Starting a 32-bit thread establishes a user-mode trap frame with cleared GS and FS, user data selectors for data and stack, user code selector, requested instruction and stack addresses, and interrupt-enable set.

Writeable shadow-stack control requires user shadow-stack hardware support and an already enabled shadow stack, otherwise it fails with not-supported or permission errors. It is idempotent when the requested state already matches, and otherwise updates the per-thread feature flag plus the user CET control register under floating-point register protection.

Shadow-stack teardown requires user shadow-stack support and is a no-op when already disabled. Otherwise it clears both CET-related control registers under floating-point register protection, frees per-thread shadow-stack resources, and clears both shadow-stack and writeable-shadow-stack feature marks.
Feature clearing removes the supplied bits from the current thread feature word without affecting other bits.
Thread-feature reset zeroes the shadow-stack control block and clears both the feature and feature-lock words in the current thread.

Extra context-switch work is skipped unless thread-flag work bits for next or previous task are set. On symmetric multiprocessor builds with conditional speculative-branch mitigation disabled, the speculation-related thread flag is masked out of both tasks before that decision.

Virtual-8086 interrupt release scans a fixed inclusive range of interrupt numbers and frees each entry whose owner matches the supplied task. Each individual free detaches the interrupt, clears the owner record, and clears the corresponding bit in a shared bitmask under an irq-saving spin lock.
A dedicated spin lock guards the shared virtual-8086 interrupt occupancy bitmask, acquired with interrupt state saved around the bit-clear operation during interrupt release.
Updates to user CET control state and the shadow-stack pointer register are serialized by acquiring the floating-point register lock with state load, then releasing it after the register writes.
A small discriminator distinguishes the two extra segment bases handled by legacy segment loading, with one value for FS and one for GS.
A name-to-offset descriptor pairs a register name with a byte offset inside the trap frame. Two helper macros build such descriptors from field names and terminate the table with a null entry.

The register translation table covers general registers and the saved trap frame comprising syscall number, instruction pointer, code segment, flags, stack pointer and stack segment. It additionally covers extended registers on 64-bit builds and data-segment registers on 32-bit builds.

Separate register-set enumerations exist for 32-bit and 64-bit tracing, covering general, floating-point, extended state, I/O permissions, TLS or shadow-stack views. Shared accessors assert that general and floating-point identifiers match across the two enumerations.

Legacy FS and GS handling distinguishes small selector values that use 64-bit thread-local storage from larger selectors that denote true segments. Zero bases with small selectors may skip the load when both sides are already zero, apply a forced reload workaround on affected AMD parts, or otherwise reload the selector; nonzero bases reload the selector only on change before writing the base register.

Protection-key state is preserved by reading the outgoing value before conditionally writing the incoming value only on change, and only when operating-system protection-key support is present. FS and GS state uses direct base writes plus conditional selector reloads when FSGSBASE is present, otherwise it delegates both segments to the legacy loader.

Common 64-bit thread start requires being called on the current trap frame, preloads user data selectors on parts with the null-segment erratum, resets CET thread features, clears FS and GS state while loading ES and DS from the caller selector, installs the new user instruction and stack addresses with code and stack selectors, marks single-step and NMI delivery enabled in FRED state when present, and sets interrupt-enable plus fixed flag bits.

The 64-bit entry uses the 64-bit code selector with user data stack and cleared data segments, while the compatibility entry keeps user data segments and selects between 64-bit and 32-bit code selectors according to the x32 request flag.

Entering 64-bit personality clears address-size restriction and compatibility status, records a 64-bit exec origin, marks vsyscall support when an address space exists, and clears the read-implies-exec personality bit. Entering 32-bit compatibility sets address-size restriction and then either clears address-space flags and compatibility status with an x32 exec origin, or sets uprobe-noted compatibility state with a 32-bit exec origin and forced 32-bit personality bits.

Linear-address-masking enablement for an address space takes effect on the current processor only when that address space is the loaded one, in which case the masking bits are ORed into the page-table base register and the per-CPU translation state is updated with the corresponding untag mask.

Register access computes a trap-frame slot from the architecture base register plus a scaled index, with compile-time checks on the base offset. Name-to-offset lookup scans linearly and reports invalid argument on no match, while offset-to-name lookup scans linearly and returns null on no match.
A selector value is considered invalid when nonzero with a privilege field different from user privilege.

On 32-bit, segment reads come from the trap frame except GS which comes from live state for the current task or saved state otherwise, and writes update the trap frame except GS which updates saved state. On 64-bit, data-segment reads and writes use live state for the current task or saved thread indices otherwise, while code and stack accesses use the trap frame.

Shadow-stack state moves from disabled to enabled shadow stack, optionally to writeable shadow stack, and back to fully disabled. Writeable state cannot be entered without the base shadow stack, disabling the base implicitly disables writeable state, and repeated requests for the current state succeed without register writes.

The 32-bit switch proceeds through floating-point switch, GS save, TLS load, extra thread-flag work, paravirtual end-of-switch, kernel stack and sysenter refresh with top-of-stack update, conditional GS restore, current-task publication, and cache-allocation notification.

The 64-bit switch proceeds through floating-point switch, FS and GS save, TLS load, paravirtual end-of-switch, DS and ES switch, FSGSBASE or legacy segment load, protection-key load, current-task and stack publication, extra thread-flag work, a system-return stack-selector fixup on affected parts, cache-allocation notification, and an AMD workload-history reset when supported.

The 32-bit switch must avoid operations that can sleep or wake tasks, with GS saved before TLS loads to avoid transient non-reloadable segments. Thread teardown treats a lingering address space as a bug on 32-bit and a warning on 64-bit, and the 64-bit switch warns under debug entry if invoked while the hard-interrupt stack is marked in use.

Segment updates through tracing must reject operation on the current task, reject selectors with non-user privilege, and reject null code or stack selectors. The 64-bit switch additionally forces a null or unexpected stack selector to the kernel data selector to avoid a system-return erratum, and thread start preloads user data selectors where zeroing would not clear the base.
The linear-address-masking user-mode width for the larger mode is six bits.
The 32-bit traceable flag mask comprises carry, parity, auxiliary, zero, sign, trap, direction, overflow, resume and alignment-check. The 64-bit mask adds nested-task.
